source_metadata.title: REWARD—an open-source framework for identifying the unknown benefits of existing medications to inform drug discovery, development, and repurposing
source_metadata.journal: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
source_metadata.source_type: methods/software framework article with applied system-scale results and summaries of prior REWARD analyses

atoms.canonical_statement: REWARD was established to perform large-scale analyses intended to identify potential benefits of existing medications beyond their original indications.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The REWARD framework was established to perform large-scale analytics on medication benefits beyond their original indications.

atoms.canonical_statement: The article aims to enable researchers to implement, validate, and extend REWARD using their own OMOP-mapped data sources.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Our goal is to enable the broader research community to implement, validate, and extend the framework using their own OMOP-mapped data sources.

atoms.canonical_statement: REWARD supports both medication-to-all-outcomes and outcome-to-all-medications questions by evaluating drug-outcome associations in an all-by-all framework.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The ability to look at research questions in either of these directions is achieved by examining drug-outcome associations in an “all-by-all” context.

atoms.canonical_statement: RxNorm is used to define 14,466 drug-ingredient exposure concepts in the REWARD universe.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The RxNorm vocabulary is used to identify drug ingredients (N = 14 466).

atoms.canonical_statement: ATC hierarchy level 4 is used to define 939 drug classes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) vocabulary to define drug classes (N = 939 at the chosen hierarchy level of 4)

atoms.canonical_statement: Pre-computed drug eras define exposure periods; first exposure is the index date, and analyzed exposure time begins one day later and continues until discontinuation or censoring.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: pre-computed drug eras are used to define exposure periods. The time of first exposure to a medication serves as the index date for all analyses examining that drug

atoms.canonical_statement: SNOMED is used to define 160,955 condition concepts as candidate outcomes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The SNOMED vocabulary is used to define all outcomes (N = 160 955 conditions).

outcome.definition: Candidate condition outcomes drawn from SNOMED concepts.

atoms.canonical_statement: Each SNOMED condition is instantiated with three outcome variants: one diagnosis, at least two diagnoses, and either an inpatient diagnosis or at least two diagnoses from other places of service.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: requiring presence of a single diagnosis; requiring 2 or more diagnoses for the same condition; and requiring either a diagnosis from an inpatient hospitalization or 2 or more diagnoses from any other place of service.

outcome.definition: Single diagnosis; at least two diagnoses; or inpatient diagnosis/at least two non-inpatient diagnoses.

atoms.canonical_statement: REWARD primarily evaluates incident outcomes, with the first occurrence of an outcome used as the outcome date.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Incident outcomes are the primary focus of REWARD and the first occurrence of an outcome is defined as the outcome date.

outcome.definition: First observed occurrence defines the outcome date.

atoms.canonical_statement: The software permits custom exposure and outcome cohort definitions, including formulation-specific exposures and more complex outcome logic or code sets.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the REWARD software allows the researchers to include additional custom exposure and outcome cohort definitions.

atoms.canonical_statement: REWARD implements two complementary causal designs: a self-controlled cohort design and an active comparator new-user design.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: There are 2 distinct and complimentary causal methods that are implemented in REWARD, the self-controlled cohort (SCC) design and the active comparator new-user (ACNU) design.

atoms.canonical_statement: The SCC design compares outcome occurrence during drug exposure with an immediately preceding equal-duration unexposed period in the same patient.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: an exposed period within each individual’s longitudinal record is compared with an immediately preceding, equal duration unexposed period.

atoms.canonical_statement: The SCC design is vulnerable to time-varying confounding and protopathic bias, particularly when the treatment indication is itself a risk factor for the outcome.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the SCC design is susceptible to time-varying confounding and protopathic bias, particularly when the indication for a drug is itself a risk factor for the outcome of interest.

atoms.canonical_statement: The ACNU design compares new users of a target drug with new users of an active comparator and uses large-scale propensity-score matching to control measured confounding.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The ACNU design, by contrast, offers stronger causal inference by explicitly controlling for measured confounding through large-scale propensity score (LSPS) matching.

atoms.canonical_statement: Because of computational burden and the need to select a comparator, ACNU is used selectively in a one-by-all rather than fully automated all-by-all mode.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: it is only deployed in a “one-by-all” manner–a single exposure of interest is examined against a comparator to analyze associations with all outcomes.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors position SCC results as hypothesis-generating signals and ACNU results as hypothesis refinement with greater causal rigor for prioritized pairs.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: results from the SCC design can be interpreted as hypothesis-generating signals while those from the ACNU design can be considered as hypothesis refinement.

atoms.canonical_statement: When both designs are applied to the same drug-outcome pair, concordant findings are treated as strengthening causal inference, whereas discordance warrants careful interpretation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: When both designs are applied to the same drug-outcome pair, concordance of results across designs strengthens causal inference.

atoms.canonical_statement: In SCC analyses, exposure continues until discontinuation or observation end with a 30-day refill gap allowance; the equal-length control period immediately precedes index, and the index date is excluded from both periods.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: An exposure period is defined as the period from initiation of a given medication until discontinuation or end of observation, allowing for a 30-day gap between the end of a medication dispensing’s supply and the subsequent refill.

atoms.canonical_statement: The SCC effect measure is an incidence rate ratio computed as exposed-period incidence divided by unexposed-period incidence; values below 1 indicate fewer incident outcomes during exposure.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: An incidence rate ratio (IRR) is then calculated as IRe+ divided by IRe−.

atoms.canonical_statement: ACNU follow-up is reserved for prioritized hypotheses, including SCC signals, a priori mechanistic interest, analogs of drugs in development, and repurposing opportunities.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The selection of a drug for ACNU analysis is typically driven by one or more of the following criteria:

atoms.canonical_statement: The ACNU large-scale propensity-score model can include tens of thousands of covariates spanning demographics, diagnoses, medication use, procedures, measurements, and healthcare utilization, with L1-regularized modeling and 1:1 matching.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The number of covariates varies depending on exposure and database being studied, but generally tens of thousands of covariates are included. A regression model using L1 regularization (LASSO regression) is used for the modeling and 1:1 matching is conducted.

atoms.canonical_statement: REWARD considers standardized mean differences of 0.10 or less well balanced after propensity-score adjustment; analyses are terminated within a database if adequate overlap or covariate balance cannot be achieved.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Covariates are considered well balanced between cohorts if the standardized difference of means is ≤0.10.

atoms.canonical_statement: ACNU uses Cox proportional-hazards models conditioned on the propensity-score match, reports calibrated and uncalibrated estimates with 95% confidence intervals, and uses calibrated results for inference.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cox proportional hazard models are used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs).

atoms.canonical_statement: Both SCC and ACNU use empirical calibration based on automatically selected negative-control outcomes to account for residual systematic bias.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In both the SCC and ACNU designs, empirical calibration is used to adjust for potential unobserved confounding and residual bias.

atoms.canonical_statement: The negative-control distribution is expected to center on an effect estimate of 1.0 with about 5% of results statistically different from the null at P<.05; the observed distribution is then used to calibrate outcome-model results.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The distribution of results is expected to have an average effect estimate of 1.0 (no association) with approximately 5% of results being statistically different from the null effect based on a P-value < .05.

atoms.canonical_statement: REWARD can run on any OMOP-mapped data source; prior applications used MarketScan Commercial, Medicare, and Medicaid, Optum Clinformatics, JMDC claims, and HealthVerity Comprehensive Claims, with meta-analysis across databases when multiple sources are used.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The REWARD framework can be used with any data source that has been mapped to the OMOP common data model.

atoms.canonical_statement: A typical REWARD benefit filter requires IRR or HR below 0.70, corresponding to at least a 30% protective association.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: include only results that have IRR (or HR) < 0.70, ie, results showing at least a 30% protective effect

atoms.canonical_statement: A typical REWARD filter requires statistical significance at P<.05.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: include only statistically significant results based on P < .05

atoms.canonical_statement: A typical REWARD filter requires the protective-effect and P-value criteria to be met in at least two databases.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: only include results where the first 2 criteria are met in at least 2 databases.

atoms.canonical_statement: An optional heterogeneity filter can remove signals showing an increased-risk estimate above a threshold such as IRR or HR greater than 2.0 in at least one database.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: An additional criterion removing any results that show an increased risk of the outcome above a certain threshold (eg, IRR [or HR] > 2.0) in at least one database may also be applied

atoms.canonical_statement: After automated filtering, REWARD results undergo manual review to remove likely protopathic findings and assess biological plausibility using clinical expertise and external preclinical or clinical evidence.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: After applying the aforementioned filtering criteria, results require manual review.

atoms.canonical_statement: REWARD is intended to narrow a large hypothesis space so prioritized exposure-outcome pairs can be studied with more tailored observational or clinical designs and combined with other evidence such as multi-omics.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: REWARD results can be used to narrow an investigator’s focus on an individual exposure-outcome pair.

atoms.canonical_statement: REWARD architecture has three primary components around a central database: protocol specification, analytics execution, and data aggregation/exploration.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: REWARD system architecture built around the central REWARD database.

atoms.canonical_statement: Aggregated non-patient-level results are stored in PostgreSQL, and exported intermediate CSV files are retained for privacy and licensing review.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Aggregated, non-patient level results are stored and explored in a PostgreSQL database. All exported data are saved as intermediate CSV files

atoms.canonical_statement: REWARD is implemented in R, depends on the OHDSI HADES library and Java, and is built from OHDSI capabilities and packages.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Code for REWARD was written in R and depends on the OHDSI HADES library, which in turn requires Java.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Each of the included conditions is used to define 3 outcome variants ... This results in nearly 7 billion potential unique exposure-outcome pairs.

atoms.canonical_statement: The current REWARD instance assesses exposure-outcome pairs across six data sources and performs meta-analysis across sources; the authors estimate the theoretical output at approximately 50 billion effect sizes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: These exposure-outcome pairs are assessed in every available data source (n = 6 in the current REWARD instance) and a meta-analysis is conducted to combine data across all sources.

atoms.canonical_statement: REWARD dashboards allow users to select exposures and outcomes, inspect database-level and meta-analytic results, forest plots, calibrated and uncalibrated estimates, calibration plots, and adjust filtering thresholds.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: To assist with navigating and digesting the large set of results, dashboards are created for each research question.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors identify disease-mechanism insight for novel intervention development as a primary REWARD use case.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Results of REWARD can provide insights into disease etiology and mechanisms to inform new drug development.

atoms.canonical_statement: REWARD can use real-world evidence from mechanistically similar approved drugs to inform additional indications for molecules still in clinical development.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: RWE can identify potential additional indications for molecules in clinical development prior to approval.

atoms.canonical_statement: REWARD is intended to identify repurposing opportunities in which an already approved medication may be applied to a different disease.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the goal is to find diseases for which an already approved medication can be applied.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors describe REWARD as differentiated by open-source implementation, standardized OMOP vocabularies for cross-database portability, and integration of pharmacoepidemiologic methods including empirical calibration and large-scale propensity scores.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: REWARD is distinguished from prior work in this space by its open-source implementation, its use of standardized OMOP CDM vocabularies enabling cross-database portability, and its integration of best-practice pharmacoepidemiologic methods

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors state that REWARD is better suited to hypothesis generation and refinement than to definitive hypothesis testing because the scalable framework uses a one-size-fits-all analytic approach.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The REWARD approach is best suited to hypothesis generation and refinement rather than hypothesis testing.

atoms.canonical_statement: SCC requires substantial manual curation because of protopathic bias and time-varying confounding, while ACNU scalability is limited by comparator selection and computationally intensive propensity-score modeling.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The SCC design, while efficient, is more susceptible to protopathic bias and time-varying confounding than the ACNU design

atoms.canonical_statement: The manuscript describes the current software instantiation as REWARD v1.0.0 and anticipates future automated comparator selection, more scalable propensity-score methods, and additional study designs.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the current software instantiation described here (v1.0.0).

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors acknowledge that REWARD analyses remain susceptible to chance findings, confounding, and information bias despite calibration, filtering, design choices, and manual review.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: REWARD analyses are not immune to the possibilities of chance findings or spurious associations arising from confounding or information bias.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors conclude that OMOP-mapped healthcare systems can implement the open-source REWARD package to generate hypotheses about drug benefits and unmet medical needs.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: REWARD is built on the OMOP CDM and any large healthcare system that maps their data to OMOP can implement the REWARD package.

source_metadata.title: REWARD—an open-source framework for identifying the unknown benefits of existing medications to inform drug discovery, development, and repurposing
source_metadata.journal: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
source_metadata.source_type: methods/software framework article with applied system-scale results and summaries of prior REWARD analyses

extraction_limitations: The current article is primarily a methods/software-framework paper. Published examples 1-3 summarize previously published REWARD analyses; those atoms are tagged reported_prior_REWARD_example and should not be treated as newly generated primary results of this manuscript.

Figure 4 contains an internal labeling inconsistency: the right-hand diagram specifies a ≥1000-patient threshold, while the printed caption repeats >100 for the right-hand branch. Calculated Figure 4 atoms follow the diagram labels and flag the figure as their source.

The manuscript expands the REWARD acronym inconsistently across locations (including “REal-World Evidence and Research of Drug performance,” “REal-World Assessment and Research of Drugs,” and “REal-World Evidence and Research of Drug”). No normalization of the acronym expansion was imposed on atom content.

Figure 5(c) dashboard values were extracted from the rendered figure because the detailed numeric table is not fully represented in surrounding narrative text. Those atoms remain review_status=needs_review.

No external verification or re-analysis of claims-database results was performed. Atoms preserve source-reported claims, explicit calculations from reported counts, and source limitations without upgrading observational signals to causal findings.
